business_problem: Pinterest needed to serve vision-language AI for shopping and discovery at internet scale, but multimodal requests involving thousands of images created prefill-heavy inference, memory pressure, and routing challenges that conventional LLM infrastructure could not handle efficiently.
solution_summary: Pinterest rebuilt its multimodal serving layer on NVIDIA Blackwell and NVIDIA Dynamo so visual discovery workloads could run as a shared production platform instead of isolated model stacks. NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs provide the compute layer for Pinterest's vision-language models, while NVIDIA Dynamo orchestrates routing, disaggregated inference phases, and service integration through a common Chat Completions API. Pinterest pairs Dynamo with vLLM and a proprietary image encoder that serves precomputed visual embeddings rather than reprocessing raw pixels on every request. That design allows the Pinterest Assistant and other product surfaces such as rerankers, content safety, OCR, and signal generation to share the same serving foundation. The platform also uses AI Configurator, DynoSim, and Dynamo Planner to simulate deployment options, optimize parallelism, and autoscale compute against latency SLAs as traffic changes.

data_flow: User search, shopping, and conversational requests enter Pinterest Assistant or other product surfaces, proprietary image embeddings and visual context are routed through Dynamo and vLLM on Blackwell GPUs, the serving layer combines text and image understanding in real time, and the resulting multimodal outputs flow back into discovery, ads, and safety experiences.
business_outcome: Pinterest scaled multimodal AI across a 14,000-GPU fleet, cut inference transaction costs to less than 8 percent of prior closed-model costs, improved ad click-through rates by 6 percent, processed 25x more visual context per request, and accelerated end-to-end latency by up to 44x for Pinterest Assistant.

The result is an end-to-end generative AI serving platform centered on Dynamo, with vLLM as the inference engine that Pinterest's teams across the company can now build on through a common Chat Completions API.
Pinterest achieves inference transaction costs at less than 8% of comparable closed proprietary models.
